'''Eicher Motors Limited''' is an Indian [[multinational corporation|multinational]] [[automotive industry|automotive company]] that manufactures [[motorcycle]]s and [[commercial vehicle]]s, headquartered in [[New Delhi]]. Eicher is the [[parent company]] of [[Royal Enfield]], a manufacturer of middleweight motorcycles. It also manufactures Eicher branded trucks and buses, under a joint venture with [[Volvo|Volvo Group]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=VE Commercial Vehicles Ltd. |url=https://www.vecv.in/ |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=www.vecv.in}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Eicher Multi-Axle 2015 Tamil Nadu.JPG|thumb|An Eicher multi-axle Torres Tempo]]

Eicher Motors Limited, the Indian company, is a commercial vehicle manufacturer in India. It traces its origins to the Goodearth Company, established in 1948 to sell and service imported tractors in India. In 1958, Eicher Tractor Corporation of India was established to manufacture tractors in India by Goodearth Company in collaboration with [[Eicher tractor|Eicher Tractors]] of Germany.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eicher Motors Ltd: A Journey Of Successful Turnarounds |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/leadership/eicher-motors-ltd-a-journey-of-successful-turnarounds/93970/1 |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=Forbes India |language=en}}</ref> The company manufactured its first indigenous tractor in 1959, and a year later changed its name to Eicher Tractors India Ltd.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eicher :: Eicher Motors Limited :: About Us :: Success Story :: Milestones |url=https://eicher.in/about-us/milestones |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=eicher.in}}</ref>

Since 1965, Eicher in India has been completely owned by Indian shareholders. The German [[Eicher tractor]] was partly owned by [[Massey Ferguson]] from 1970, when they bought 30%. Massey Ferguson bought out the German company in 1973.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eicher Motors Share Price Today Live Updates: Eicher Motors Sees Marginal Decline in Price, EMA5 Reflects Recent Trend |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/stock-liveblog/eicher-motors-share-price-today-live-updates-07-may-2024/liveblog/109901370.cms |access-date= |website=The Economic Times |language=en}}</ref>

In 2005, Eicher Motors Ltd sold their tractors and engines business to [[Tractors and Farm Equipment Limited|TAFE Tractors]] (Tractors and Farm Equipment Ltd) of [[Chennai]], the Indian [[licensee]] of [[Massey Ferguson]] tractors.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2005-05-26 |title=Tafe buys Eicher's tractor, engine & gear businesses for Rs 310 crore |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tafe-buys-eichers-tractor-engine-gear-businesses-for-rs-310-crore/articleshow/1122079.cms |access-date=2024-09-21 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

In October 1982, a collaboration agreement with [[Mitsubishi]] for the manufacture of light commercial vehicles (LCVs) was signed in Tokyo and in the same period the incorporation of Eicher Motors Limited also took place. LCVs were sold under the "Eicher Mitsubishi" brand. In February 1990, Eicher Goodearth bought 26% stake in [[Enfield India]] Ltd and by 1993 Eicher acquired a majority stake (60% equity shareholding) in Royal Enfield India.

In July 2008, Eicher Motors Limited (EML) and [[Volvo|Volvo Group]]'s formed a 50:50 joint venture called VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV) which designs, manufactures and markets commercial vehicles, engineering components and provides engineering design.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DHNS |title=Volvo set to trim Eicher Motors exposure again |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/business/volvo-set-trim-eicher-motors-2131980 |access-date=2024-09-21 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref>
[[File:Eicher truck.jpg|thumb|An Eicher [[garbage truck|Garbage Tempo]] transporting [[municipal solid waste]]]]

At present, Volvo Group owns 45.6% of VECV,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.volvogroup.com/content/dam/volvo/volvo-group/markets/global/en-en/investors/reports-and-presentations/annual-reports/annual-and-sustainability-report-2016.pdf |pages=74 |title=Annual and Sustainability Report 2016 |publisher=Volvo |access-date=12 August 2017 |archive-date=2 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702031810/http://www.volvogroup.com/content/dam/volvo/volvo-group/markets/global/en-en/investors/reports-and-presentations/annual-reports/annual-and-sustainability-report-2016.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> while Eicher Motors holds the remaining 54.4%.<ref>{{cite news |title=Investor Presentation May 2022 |url=https://www.eicher.in/uploads/1652449394_eicher-motors-earnings-presentation-for-4Q-%26-FY2021-22.pdf |access-date=16 February 2023 |work=Eicher Motors |page=47 |archive-date=19 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319162312/https://www.eicher.in/uploads/1652449394_eicher-motors-earnings-presentation-for-4Q-%26-FY2021-22.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2020, VECV bought [[Volvo Buses]] India operations for [[Indian Rupees|₹]]100 [[crore]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Mishra|first=Lalatendu|date=2020-08-13|title=Eicher Motor subsidiary to buy Volvo India's bus business for ₹100 crore|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/eicher-motors-buys-volvo-indias-bus-business/article32343637.ece|access-date=2021-01-09|issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

In 2012, Eicher Motors started a [[joint venture]] with American company [[Polaris Inc.|Polaris Industries]] called Eicher Polaris to make personal utility vehicles, starting with [[Eicher Polaris Multix]] in 2015. This joint venture company ceased operations in 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Eicher Motors ends JV with US-based Polaris |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/eicher-motors-ends-jv-with-us-based-polaris/articleshow/63268139.cms |access-date=16 February 2023 |work=The Times of India |date=12 March 2018}}</ref>

==Group structure==
[[File:Bangladesh Police (DMP) Eicher Pro 1055 tow-truck. (34491460656).jpg|thumb|Eicher [[Vehicle recovery|Recovery Tempo]] being used by the [[Bangladesh Police]]]]
The Eicher Group has business interests in design and development, manufacturing, and local and international marketing of trucks, buses, motorcycles, automotive gears, and components.

===VE Commercial Vehicles===
VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV) Limited is a joint venture between [[Volvo Group]] and Eicher Motors Limited. VECV is divided into six business units:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vecv.in|title=VE Commercial Vehicles Ltd.|website=www.vecv.in}}</ref>
* Eicher Trucks/(Large/Small-size Tempo) and Buses/(Large/Small-size Van) 
* Volvo Trucks (Large-Small Size Tempo) India
* Volvo Buses (Large-Small Size Van) India
* Eicher Engineering Components
* Eicher Power Solutions
* VE Powertrain

===Royal Enfield Motors===
[[Royal Enfield]], a motorcycle manufacturer, is a subsidiary of Eicher Motors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Saraiya |first=Kriti |date=March 22, 2024 |title=Eicher Motors incorporates 100% subsidiary 'Royal Enfield Europe' in Netherlands |url=https://auto.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/two-wheelers/eicher-motors-incorporates-100-subsidiary-royal-enfield-europe-in-netherlands/108713432 |access-date=June 27, 2025 |website=ETAuto.com | publisher= The Economic Times |language=en}}</ref>

==Vehicles==
*Eicher Lorge/Small-Size Tempo Trucks
*Eicher Buses/Lorge/Small-Size Vans
*Volvo Lorge/Small-Size Tempo Trucks
*Volvo Lorge/Small-Size Buses and Vans 
*[[Royal Enfield|Royal Enfield Motorcycles]]
In the end of 2025 VE Commercial Vehicles unveiled their ProX line up of new small trucks under Eicher Trucks and Buses brand. The line-up was built from ground up because VECV never had small commercial trucks in any brand. First electric variants were launched with 32 and 40kwh lithium iron phosphate battery with 107hp and 250km range. Later diesel versions were launched with their all new E449 X2 engine a 4-cylinder 2 liter coupled with 5 Speed transmission with output of 80hp and 230nm of torque. The line-up has payload capacity of 1.3 to 1.8 tons with two cargo bed length options 9.8 and 10.8ft. The cabin has sitting capacity of driver plus two pax and built with Indian and European Safety Standards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eicher Pro X Diesel: A Ground-Up Indian SCV Built for a Fast-Evolving Economy – Motorindia |url=https://www.motorindiaonline.in/eicher-pro-x-diesel-a-ground-up-indian-scv-built-for-a-fast-evolving-economy/ |access-date=2026-05-02 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Joint Ventures ==

=== VE Connected Solutions Pvt Ltd (VECS) ===
In May 2024 Volvo Eicher Commercial Vehicles Ltd started a 51:49 joint venture named VE Connected Solutions Pvt Ltd (VECS) with iTriangle Infotech Pvt Ltd a [[Bengaluru]] based [[vehicle tracking system]] company. The newly formed venture deals in [[Fleet management]], [[Fleet telematics system]], [[Driver scoring]], Vehicle tracking system, [[Fleet digitalization]] and EV mobility solutions. By July 2027 the VECV will increase its share in venture from 51 to 74% for 11.01 million Indian rupees.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eicher Arm VECV To Raise Stake In Connected Solutions JV To 74% |url=https://www.autocarpro.in/news/eicher-arm-vecv-to-raise-stake-in-connected-solutions-jv-to-74-percent-132671 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=Autocar Professional |language=en}}</ref>

=== Volvo Financial Services (VFS) ===
Eicher Motors announces a new joint venture with [[Volvo Financial Services]]. In May 2026, Eicher Motors Limited announced a 50:50 joint venture with Volvo Financial Services (VFS) to provide financing, leasing, and other financial services for Volvo and Eicher-branded commercial vehicles in India. Eicher Motors approved an investment of up to ₹750 crore for a 50% equity stake in Volvo Financial Services India. The joint venture will serve as the captive financing arm for VECV, Eicher Motors, Volvo Group, and [[Royal Enfield]] products.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-10 |title=Volvo Financial Services and Eicher Motors Limited announce joint venture for financial services in India |url=https://www.volvogroup.com/en/news-and-media/news/2026/may/volvo-financial-services-and-eicher-motors-limited-announce-joint-venture-for-financial-services-in-india.html |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=www.volvogroup.com |language=en}}</ref>
